Two required properties: (1) a subtle overall WARM colour cast lies across the whole image, as if white-balanced too warm; (2) the pale background and the lightest parts of the mark are BLOWN OUT / CLIPPED to the very top of the tonal range, effectively pure near-white with absolutely no recoverable tonal detail in the highlights, so any attempt to pull the highlights down would change nothing. assets.prompt: A daylight photograph taken by a window of an old cream card lying on a natural linen cloth. Foil-blocked in the centre of the card is an interlocked MONOGRAM of the letters M and S, their strokes woven together so they share small ENCLOSED COUNTERS (the interior holes where the two letters overlap). The monogram is bright metallic FOIL that acts like a mirror: its apparent colour is not a single hue but a mix of soft daylight blue-grey and warm window reflections picked up from the room, so its colour cannot be trusted. The cream CARD stock itself is an even, clean, neutral warm cream (#EFE9DC) lit softly by north daylight, the truest neutral in the frame. The linen cloth is a muted stone (#C9BEA8). Slight soft shadow, gentle daylight, realistic snapshot. No printed text on the card other than the foil monogram.

assets.content:
MAISON SERAULT - PACKAGING ARTWORK REQUIREMENTS
From the new box supplier and the engraver. Treat every figure as a hard limit.

BOX SUPPLIER (foil blocking on dark stock)
  Box stock: Boutique Charcoal (#2A2724), a very dark uncoated board.
  Foil: Warm Brass (#B08D4C).
  Foil spread allowance: 0.15mm. Foil spreads outward into the stock on press, so the reversed/knock-out artwork must be drawn to allow for it or fine counters close.
  Minimum foil stroke on the dark stock: 0.30mm at final size. Anything thinner fills in.
  Clear space around the mark: 6mm on all sides, minimum.
  Box face panel: 90mm x 90mm.

  RIBBON
  Ribbon width: 10mm. The wordmark runs ALONG the ribbon.
  Wordmark used width on the ribbon: 60mm long, so cap height works out to roughly 7mm.
  Same 0.30mm minimum stroke applies on the ribbon.

ENGRAVER (clasp plates)
  Requires a SINGLE CLOSED OUTLINE of each mark, one path, counters present as true holes, not a filled picture.
  Minimum engraved cut width: 0.25mm at final size.
  Clasp plate area for the monogram: 8mm x 8mm.

CARD (the enclosure card, foil on cream)
  Card: 100mm x 70mm on Card Cream (#EFE9DC).
  Monogram used size on the card: about 18mm.

assets.content:
LAYOUT SPEC for the card printer's existing enclosure-card press PDF (flat, single record; to be reverse-engineered into a live merge template downstream).

Document: single enclosure card, 100 x 70 mm LANDSCAPE, NO bleed box present (trim = media box, 0 mm bleed), fonts embedded. This is the file the card printer has run by hand, one card at a time, for years; it is the artwork for ONE piece.

WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE PRINTED (apparent blocks):
- Top centre: the house MONOGRAM foil-blocked, about 18 mm across.
- Upper left: the PIECE NAME in the house serif, large.
- Under it: a REFERENCE + METAL line in a small companion face (e.g. 'SER-R-09  .  18ct Yellow Gold').
- Lower left: the PRICE.
- Right: a small square PICTURE of the piece.
- Bottom strip: the house CARE LINE in small type.

HOW IT IS ACTUALLY SET (the reverse-engineering trap):
- The PIECE NAME, the REFERENCE + METAL line and the PRICE are a SINGLE continuous text story in ONE text frame (name, a forced line break, the reference and metal, a forced line break, the price), NOT three addressable frames. Downstream they can only be reached by position inside that one story, paragraph by paragraph, not frame by frame.
- The MONOGRAM at the head is the card printer's OWN crude redrawn tracing, held as a GROUP OF VECTOR PATHS, NOT a picture/graphic frame and NOT the recovered master. It must be REPLACED with the recovered monogram, not reused, and it is not somewhere a picture can be bound.
- The one genuine rectangular PICTURE/GRAPHIC FRAME on the card is the small piece window on the right; that is where the per-piece photograph binds.
- The CARE LINE is its own separate short story.
- The sample carries BAKED text from the card it was set for: PIECE NAME 'Serault Signet', REFERENCE 'SER-R-09' (an abandoned short numbering, since replaced by references like SER-R-014-YG on the current list) and PRICE '$1,650'. None of it matches the current collection list, so the template's own words must be REPLACED, not trusted.

NO BLEED: because the media box equals the trim and no bleed box exists, a press-ready-with-bleed delivery cannot be honoured from anything derived from this file, however the render is called.

FIELD LABELS the downstream mapping must resolve (present as content, not visible tokens): PIECE_NAME | REFERENCE | METAL | PRICE | CARE_LINE | PIECE_PICTURE

Colours: Card Cream #EFE9DC ground, Serault Ink #1B2A2E for the name, reference and price, Warm Brass #B08D4C foil monogram, Soft Stone #C9BEA8 hairline rule.
